# Maximize Sum of At Most K Distinct Elements.

@example 40 occurs twice but can be taken only once; 25 and 12 are the next largest values.
[12,40,7,40,25,3]
3
=> [40,25,12]

@example nums holds only two different values, so only two entries can be taken.
[6,2,6,2,6]
4
=> [6,2]

@example With k = 1, take the largest value.
[15,8,31]
1
=> [31]

# The smallest input.
[1]
1
=> [1]

# All entries equal: a single value, whatever k is.
[9,9,9,9]
4
=> [9]

# The largest value three times: the three largest entries would be
# 50, 50, 50, and removing repeats from those leaves only one value.
[50,50,50,49,48,47]
3
=> [50,49,48]

# Repeats inside the top values, with enough different values below.
[10,9,9,8,8,7,6]
4
=> [10,9,8,7]

# Fewer different values than k, but more than one.
[2,2,3,3]
3
=> [3,2]

# k = n with many repeats.
[4,7,4,7,4,7,1,1]
8
=> [7,4,1]

# k = n, all different: the whole array, from largest to smallest.
[11,3,8,20,5,14,1]
7
=> [20,14,11,8,5,3,1]

# Sorted from smallest to largest in nums; the answer goes the other way.
[1,2,3,4,5]
2
=> [5,4]

# Values near 10^9, 1 apart; their sum would not fit in an int.
[999999999,1000000000,999999998,1000000000,1]
3
=> [1000000000,999999999,999999998]

# The largest value twice, and nothing else.
[1000000000,1000000000]
2
=> [1000000000]

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[211846738,211846738,637538261,211846738,211846738,637538261,637538261]
1
=> [637538261]

@gen 3 small
[5,2,1,4,4,4,5,1]
1
=> [5]

@gen 4 small
[999999999,999999998,999999998,999999997]
4
=> [999999999,999999998,999999997]

@gen 5 small
[645874140,837186695,837186695,165482840,165482840,165482840]
6
=> [837186695,645874140,165482840]

@gen 9 small
[1,6,1,1,6,3,3]
7
=> [6,3,1]

@gen 10 small
[999999998,1000000000,999999997,999999997,999999999,999999999,999999998,999999997]
5
=> [1000000000,999999999,999999998,999999997]

@gen 11 small
[3,2,2,1,5,1,3]
3
=> [5,3,2]
